Work · the back office

65 screens for the person at the desk. Every drawing is the real DOM captured from the running app at 1440, scaled as a unit and never reflowed — including where the code breaks a rule, because a drawing that shows the rule instead launders a violation into something that looks shipped.

00 · How to read this

This page is written for a build lane to read instead of a conversation. It answers, for the clerk's side of Work: what screens exist, whether a clerk can reach them, what runs behind each one, what the product refuses to do, what we are committing to build, and in what order.

Its companion is the field app document, which carries the technician's 50 screens and 125 capabilities. Neither is the whole picture and each says so.

MarkMeans
TASKCommitted work with a plan id Pn.m. Build it.
TODAYWhat the code does now, with a file and line. Do not re-derive it.
GAPA defect or a missing piece. Information only unless a TASK sits beside it.
RULEDA Product Owner decision with its date. Binding. Never re-ask it.
OPENNobody has answered. Never resolve one by choosing a value — stub with the id.
SOURCEWhere a control's values come from. See §01.
Two things this document exists to catch

A route existing is not a door. Almost every test asks whether a screen renders at its own address — the one place a door is not needed. Nothing asks whether a clerk standing somewhere else can get to it. This document found nine capabilities whose backend already exists and whose screen carries no control, and one row action that opens the wrong screen entirely.

A description commits nobody. Saying a thing is missing is not undertaking to build it — which is why GAP and TASK are different marks and are counted separately.

Thirty-six rulings of 23 and 24 September 2026, and none is in the repository yet

The tab formerly called Awaiting approval is Approvals. ⚠ The i18n key namespace is already work.approvals.*, so 23 keys need no change — but eleven catalogue values do, and B14 rule 35 says each is written in its own language rather than translated from English. The address and the endpoint stay: no clerk reads a URL.

A number I got wrong, corrected here rather than quietly

This paragraph said eleven until the pre-publish pass re-derived it from the capability register and got nine. The brief requires every number stated in prose to be re-derived before publishing, and this is what that check is for — the wrong figure had already been written twice before anything counted it. The nine are B11, F4, F5, F8, F16, F22, F23 and the two halves of the task/material row edit.

The manifest at the foot of this page is generated from the assembled HTML, never written by hand. A screen with no class, or a task with no id, is simply absent from it — which makes its absence visible.

01 · Standards

StandardWhat it means here
Draw from the codeEvery drawing below is the real captured DOM of the running app, rendered under the product's own stylesheet. Fidelity was measured, not eyeballed: 80 properties identical, 0 differing across 8 elements × 10 properties. Where the code breaks a rule, the drawing shows the code and the breach is filed — see 1·1, whose create renders outlined and below the pager.
One 1440 windowDesktop only, scaled as a unit, never reflowed. Scale is clientWidth / 1440, capped at 1 and floored at 0.42, with the scaled height reserved. Measured from documentElement.clientWidth — never 100vw, which includes the scrollbar and manufactures the overflow it is meant to prevent.
Measured tokensRead from tokens.css. Radius is 0px at every step, so everything is square. Archivo, heading weight 800, page head 32px.
Drawings do not re-themeThe document follows your theme; the drawings are pictures of a light product and stay light.
Use the product's own componentA multi-step flow is drawn as the shared WizardFrame where it uses one. ⚠ Three of Work's four do; the rule builder does not, and its drawing shows the hand-rolled stepper it actually has.

What passes, and is worth saying

Rule 31 on visible ids — order detail addresses by WO-0001, the technician page by the slug d-ortiz, templates by ST-0003. Every screen that could have shown a uuid does not — except the one that asks a person to type one.

Money — every figure in the module renders at two decimals: $6.40, $92.40, $25.96, $181.73. Nothing interpolates a raw amount.

Rule 34's vocabulary — Recorded appears on the Performance cost tile, correctly.

Rule 21 — the drawings in this document are Tailwind-free by construction, and the module's own components are utility-based. No violation found.

Icons for row actions, one table type, two button sizes — the 👁/✎ pattern and the single DataTable are used consistently across all seven lists.

The two traps, both live in this register

A SIGNED enum with a deliberate hole. Dispatch state is seven values behind a database CHECK constraint — adding an eighth is a migration, not a constant. Outcome is five with a rule id, and Bulk act is three in BULK_ACTS: a fourth is a backend change, however obvious it looks on a toolbar.

A control that is a literal today and should not be. Job type and Premises are free-text boxes on 1·4a — and both already have a real source. A lane drawing that screen would naturally hardcode a handful of job types; the model has nine, with 21 sub-types on the demo.

02 · Development plan

Seven increments, each shippable on its own. No dates — the order comes from what depends on what, and from putting the cheapest value first. A phase that cannot answer what can a clerk newly do is a phase nobody can sign off, so every one of them answers it.

Why P1 is “stop losing work” rather than “raise a job”

P1 carries no migration at all — every fault in it is a screen discarding something the backend already returns correctly. It is the cheapest phase in the plan and the one a clerk feels most, so it goes first even though P2 is the more obvious headline.

What will bite

RiskWhy, and where it lands
A green suite proves nothingNo gate in this repository reads rendered output. A create button in the wrong tier and in the wrong place passed every test, and so did a row action opening the wrong screen. Six of this document's findings came from driving the app and from nothing else.
The test database hides a class of failureconfig/settings/test.py hardcodes in-memory sqlite. A failed statement aborts a PostgreSQL transaction and does not abort a sqlite one — so a bulk act that catches and continues passes everywhere and loses the batch in production. The bulk path already gets this right, with one savepoint per order; anything added beside it must too.
A hold outlives its reasonTwo controls on 2·1 still refuse over screens that shipped in wave H, and the parts Issue log is greyed over an endpoint that exists. Write the test that fires when the hold expires, in the same commit as the hold, asserting the destination by address and by screen id.
Two answers to one questionThe beta reported filter not working; the code walk measured five chips reading in SQL. Both are right — an empty result from a working filter is indistinguishable from a broken one. Resolving that by believing either side alone would have wasted the fix.
Immutability is not a conventionwork_order_assignments is append-only by database trigger, not discipline. P4.4's reassign-as-one-act must add a row, never update one.
A migration with no way backP0.3's CHECK constraint on hold reasons makes every later value a migration. Decide the list before writing the constraint, or state the rollback.
A ruling that reverses a signed ruleP4.5 reverses BR-WRK-029 at the write. US-WRK-020 TC-4 asserts the old behaviour and goes red by design — that redness is the proof it landed, and a lane that "fixes" the test has undone the ruling.

The filter contradiction, and how it resolves

The beta walk reported filter not working; the code walk measured five chips reading in SQL. Both are right. Filtering by priority correctly returns nothing, because no order has one — an empty result from a working filter is indistinguishable from a broken one. Task P1.5 seeds priorities.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the checklist shows on a job that is not completed too — as the plan

PO, answering the question this page put: “it should be showned to the uncompleted also”. So the Checklist tab is on both shapes. Before completion it is the plan — the safety lines, the tasks with their minutes and which need a photograph, the readings to take, the help. After completion it is the record — who did each line and when, the values, the photographs. The signature still shows only once the job is completed. Said again the same afternoon, on the published copy, which still showed the old shape: “here the checklist screen should be visible to the not completed orders also - user should know the order details”. Nothing new was asked. The copy was out of date because this change was built and not yet published.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the back office never completes a job — it only accepts

PO, verbatim: “The signed flow is that the technician completes the job and the office accepts it. - this is correct” and “back office cannot complete the job it can only accept it”. So Mark complete leaves the order page, Complete leaves the edit page's Status list, and the checklist's tick boxes leave the desk. ⚠ The server must say so too: today the completion endpoint accepts a field result from any role in the utility — its own comment reads “the FIELD reports” — so a hidden button would not stop an office user (hard-won law 1). It answers the question left open on this page earlier today.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the order page changes with its status

PO, on 1·2a: “this screen should have viriations depending on the status. if the order is comleted then only user can view details in checklist and can view the customer signature and photos. if not completed then that data should not be visible.” And on 1·2b: “the back office user will be viewing the details of the workorder which was completed by technician.” So there are two shapes. Not completed: Overview, Parts and Audit — no Checklist tab, no signature, no photographs. Completed: Overview with the signature, the Checklist as a record of what the technician did, Parts and Audit.

RULED 2026-09-24 · action buttons at the top right, on every screen

PO: “in each wireframe follow the UI principles - the action buttons should be on the top right side”. It is B14 rule 2, already ratified — one page header … right-aligned actions — and the order page, the edit page and the Orders list all broke it. Two places keep their buttons at the bottom, because the same rules say so: a step-by-step flow keeps Back and Continue in its footer (rule 3), and a dialog keeps its buttons in its own footer.

Drawn on a real order raised for the purpose — because no seeded order could show all six

None of the 42 seeded orders stands on an account, so on the demo the Customer tab can only ever read Account —. So on 24 Sep a job was raised in the throwaway demo database through the product's own raise service — WO-0043, a meter exchange on account AC-2026-00001 (Ana Alvarez, 101 Silver Creek Rd, Unit 1, meter W-5000) — and assigned through the product's own dispatch act to D. Ortiz for 25 Sep, 9–12. Every tab below is that order, captured from the running app. Nothing was written to the repository.

⚠ Found while raising it: the raise accepted a water job on an electric meter

The first attempt pointed the water template Meter exchange — residential at meter E-5000 — the account's ELECTRIC meter. The raise accepted it: nothing compares a template's service with the service of the meter it is raised on. The order was re-pointed to the water meter W-5000 before any drawing was made. On 1·4a the fix is to offer only templates of the anchor's service — task P2.11.

⚠ CORRECTED 24 Sep — the phone does NOT show the customer, and this document said it did

Earlier this page, beta report #30 and the field-app document all said the phone already composes Miller, Sarah · (512) 555-0114 (mobile.py:329). It composes the line from keys it never receives. customers_seam.account() returns id, number, status and unit — no name, no phone — and mobile._customer_contact asks it for both. Run on WO-0043, whose holder is Ana Alvarez with a phone on file, it returns {name: None, phone: None, account_no: AC-2026-00001}. So on every job, the technician's tap to call has nothing to call. No test covers it — US-WRK-042 TC-5 names the line and nothing asserts it. That is why this tab needs a backend task, not just a front-end one (P1.15).

⚠ A completed job with no build cannot be accepted anywhere — measured

WO-0043 was closed as Passed on 24 Sep. It appears in Approvals, and its only action there is greyed out — This job has no build. Acceptance lives only in the new-connection drawer, so a job raised on an account, a premises or a meter — by a clerk, a rule or a move-out — can be finished and never accepted: its cost lines are never saved and its reading never becomes a meter read. Accept ✓ on this page is the one place for every job, and Approvals' View opens it (P1.5).

⚠ Closing a job does not move it to Complete — measured

After WO-0043 was closed, its chips read Scheduled · Completed: the phone's close writes the work status and never the dispatch status. On the demo, 22 finished and accepted jobs still read Queued. The drawing shows Complete, because closing a job must move it there (P1.31).

What the signature looks like today — measured on a real one

A signature was captured on WO-0043 on 24 Sep through the product's own capture: Ana Alvarez's mark and printed name. The office sees one sentence — Signed by Ana Alvarez. — on the Customer tab. The mark itself is stored and never served: the signature endpoint returns the name, the time and whether it was refused, and no link to the picture. Nor does it say who took it. To be seen, it must first be served (P1.23); the door-hanger photo on a refusal is already a normal photograph and can be linked today.

What “reviewed” means here, and what it does not

The signature is shown on the Overview at a size a person can judge, with who signed, when, and who held the phone; View opens it in the same viewer as the photographs. Accepting the job is still the Approvals step — this adds no second approval, it gives the person approving something to look at.

RULED 2026-09-24 · action buttons at the top right, on every screen

PO: “in each wireframe follow the UI principles - the action buttons should be on the top right side”. It is B14 rule 2, already ratified — one page header … right-aligned actions — and the order page, the edit page and the Orders list all broke it. Two places keep their buttons at the bottom, because the same rules say so: a step-by-step flow keeps Back and Continue in its footer (rule 3), and a dialog keeps its buttons in its own footer.

RULED 2026-09-24 · assigning and reassigning are drawn

PO, on 1·2a: “resassigned wireframe is missing and assigning the workorder wireframes are also missing”. Three drawings answer it: 1·3a assigning a job nobody has, 1·3b moving a job to someone else, and 1·1b assigning several at once from the list. All three are the product's own screens, captured 24 Sep.

Advice, never a block — how the list reads

Ruled 23 Sep: the match is a guideline for a better allocation and must never stop a job. So every name stays choosable, and beside each one is the reason it fits or does not: the skill (served today), the area, whether they are off that day, and how many jobs they already have. Best fit marks the top one. Picking against the advice records who overrode it (P4.5). The counts drawn are illustrations.

The Change effects box says the customer is told — whatever changed

It lists the customer is told the visit moved on every save; measured on a priority-only change. The box should list what THIS save will do: the technician told, the old technician told, the customer told only when the day or window moves.

⚠ THE WORST THING IN THIS DOCUMENT, AND A PERSON FOUND IT TOO

A dispatcher believes a job is assigned when it is not. The blueprint filed it from the code walk and the beta reporter hit it independently — which is the strongest argument for its priority there is.

⚠ RULED 2026-09-23 · the match advises, it never blocks

dispatch._candidate_or_refuse() re-runs the skill predicate at the write and raises work.dispatch.skill_mismatch. There is no tenant switch for it. The code's reason for checking at the write is good and survives — a rule that only lives in a picker is a rule any other caller walks straight past. What changes is the verb. Task P4.5 keeps the check, records the override and stops it raising. US-WRK-020 TC-4 asserts the opposite and goes red by design.

RULED 2026-09-24 · action buttons at the top right, on every screen

PO: “in each wireframe follow the UI principles - the action buttons should be on the top right side”. It is B14 rule 2, already ratified — one page header … right-aligned actions — and the order page, the edit page and the Orders list all broke it. Two places keep their buttons at the bottom, because the same rules say so: a step-by-step flow keeps Back and Continue in its footer (rule 3), and a dialog keeps its buttons in its own footer.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the back office never completes a job — it only accepts

PO, verbatim: “The signed flow is that the technician completes the job and the office accepts it. - this is correct” and “back office cannot complete the job it can only accept it”. So Mark complete leaves the order page, Complete leaves the edit page's Status list, and the checklist's tick boxes leave the desk. ⚠ The server must say so too: today the completion endpoint accepts a field result from any role in the utility — its own comment reads “the FIELD reports” — so a hidden button would not stop an office user (hard-won law 1). It answers the question left open on this page earlier today.

RULED 2026-09-24 · assigning and reassigning are drawn

PO, on 1·2a: “resassigned wireframe is missing and assigning the workorder wireframes are also missing”. Three drawings answer it: 1·3a assigning a job nobody has, 1·3b moving a job to someone else, and 1·1b assigning several at once from the list. All three are the product's own screens, captured 24 Sep.

⚠ The page opens an assigned job as unassigned, on the wrong day, at the wrong hour — measured

WO-0043 is D. Ortiz's for 25 Sep, 9–12. Its edit page opened reading Assigned to: Nobody yet, Date: 27 Sep and 14:00. Three causes, each read in the code: the server sends the technician's NAME and no id, so the list cannot select him — while the page's own comment says the id is sent “for exactly this reason” (hard-won law 1); the date is filled from the due date, not the appointment; and the time is the UTC hour, 14:00 for 09:00.

⚠ Changing only the time slot moved the job to another day and made it overdue — measured

On WO-0043 only the window was changed, to 12:00–17:00, and saved. The page sent the day it was showing — the due date — so the appointment moved from 25 Sep to 24 Sep, stored as 12:00–17:00 in UTC, which is 7 AM to noon in Texas, and the due time was reset to midnight UTC — the job was overdue the moment it saved. Changing only the priority, by contrast, sent only the priority: the page sends what moved, correctly — it is what it believes the job looks like that is wrong. This is P1 work: it loses a promise made to a customer.

RULED 2026-09-24 · raise in bulk, on units

PO, verbatim: “in raise a job the user should be able to raised bulk work order. the work orders should be raised on units.” So 1·4a picks the building, then its units — one job for each unit ticked. Every job names its building and its unit, because a unit alone is not an anchor: measured, the raise refuses a job that names only a unit (work.order.anchor_required). That is why Premises stays the first field.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the premises is a dropdown — one you can type into

PO, on 1·4a′: “here premise should be dropdown”. The signed rule for a long list already says how: BR-SHL-033 — any long dropdown (roughly >10 options: accounts, premises …) is always SEARCHABLE (type-ahead), never a bare scroll list. So it opens like a dropdown, with its arrow, and narrows as the clerk types. It reads the server's own search, GET /premises/picker?q= — already served, paged in SQL, and used by the service-request form — which answers each building with its type and its units: Mill Pond finds nine on the demo, and 301 Mill Pond Ln says Apartment complex · 6 units.

⚠ Measured · a unit from another building is accepted

Probed 24 Sep and rolled back: a job at Kestrel Park ph. 2 naming Unit 205 of 500 Main St was raised without a word. The raise never checks that the unit belongs to the premises, and the job would read Kestrel Park ph. 2 · Unit 205 — a unit that is not there. A bulk raise makes this easy to do forty times. P2.13.

⚠ Measured · the template's scope and service do not reach the job

Tap and service line is a per-unit water template. Raised by hand on Unit 205 it landed per premises, with no service: the raise takes scope from the request — defaulting to premises — never from the template, and copies no service at all. P2.14.

Where a job has no unit to go on — our reading, recorded rather than asked

A job for the whole building — a service drop, a mark-out — is one job on the premises whatever is ticked, because its template is done to the building. And a premises with no units — 2 of 79 in the demo, both pending — takes one job on the premises, because there is nothing else to raise it on. Overruling either is one sentence.

B18 §8.2's batching is a different door, and a bulk raise has no batch number

B18 §8.2 batches a new building's work by default — 500 Main St's 25 units make seven orders, not seventy-six. That is the plan a new connection generates. This form is a clerk raising by hand, and the ruling says one job per unit, so the two do not collide. A bulk raise is separate jobs with no batch number — ruled on 4 Sep for the bulk assign (OQ-WRK-1497, CLOSED: “three separate assignments”).

⚠ YOUR SPECIFICATION SUPERSEDES MY FIRST REMEDY, AND I AM LEAVING THE WRONG ONE VISIBLE

My earlier remedy R1 guessed at two pickers. Observation #34 names five fields with two mandatory — Job Type*, Template*, Priority, Expected Date, Description — and adds a technician at creation. R5 draws it. R1 is struck rather than deleted, because a document that quietly removes its wrong guesses teaches nobody that guessing happened.

The anchor is not optional and is not in your five

ck_work_orders_has_anchor refuses a row with no connection, premises, account or asset. So Premises* stays as the first field. That is the whole answer to how will a work order raise if we are only taking address and sub area.

⚠ Corrected on 1·4a and 1·4a′ — the job types are the demo's own

Those two drawings showed job types no picker offers — Meter exchange, New connection. They now read the demo's list: nine types and 21 sub-types — water's eighteen and electric's three — so Meter Maintenance › Meter Change and Connection › Residential Connection.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the premises is a dropdown — one you can type into

PO, on 1·4a′: “here premise should be dropdown”. The signed rule for a long list already says how: BR-SHL-033 — any long dropdown (roughly >10 options: accounts, premises …) is always SEARCHABLE (type-ahead), never a bare scroll list. So it opens like a dropdown, with its arrow, and narrows as the clerk types. It reads the server's own search, GET /premises/picker?q= — already served, paged in SQL, and used by the service-request form — which answers each building with its type and its units: Mill Pond finds nine on the demo, and 301 Mill Pond Ln says Apartment complex · 6 units.

RULED 2026-09-24 · the assets list has its own search

PO, on 1·4a′: “here there should be search for assets”. The box matches what a clerk has in front of them — the asset number, the serial, and where it is — and it names those in its placeholder, because a box that names a field it does not match is worse than no box (B14 rule 19). It searches in SQL before the page is cut, as the Orders list's box does, so it finds the asset on page 40 and not only on the page showing.

RULED 2026-09-24 · an asset type chosen means the asset must be chosen

PO, verbatim: “if asset type is selected then user needs to select asset - update the wireframes .” — said after asking what happens when a unit has two water meters, and how the technician knows which one to work on. So Asset type follows Template and offers the template's own asset types (wot_asset_types); a template that names none offers any type, or none — BR-WRK-056, the rule the asset page's door already follows. Once a type is chosen, Assets* is required: the ticked units' assets of that type and of the template's service. A unit with one is ticked for you. A unit with two or more is never guessed — the step refuses until the clerk chooses.

Measured · the two-meter case is in the demo data

At 301 Mill Pond Ln every flat has two or three water meters. Meter exchange — residential names one asset type, Meter, so its list is seven: Apt 101 carries two of that type — W-5040 in the front boundary box, last read 2,546 kgal on 11 Aug, and M-MASTER-01, recorded nowhere and never read — and the other five carry one each. The sub-meters (SM-70xx, rear alley) are type Sub-meter and are not listed. The serial number is empty on all 137 assets in the demo, so today the only thing that tells two meters apart on site is the location note — filled on 110 of 137.

⚠ The job knows its asset — no screen tells the technician

A job holds exactly one asset (work_orders.asset_id), and the reading typed on it is posted to that asset at acceptance, so the record is never ambiguous. The person is. The order page shows no asset (P1.2 adds it); the phone's job bundle carries none; and the template's Show asset card switch is saved on every job and drawn nowhere. A reading taken from the wrong meter lands on the right meter's history. The phone half is in the field-app document: the asset card, and the technician confirming the number on the meter before the first reading.

⚠ Do not copy the other premises dropdowns — they stop at 200

Add units loads the first 200 premises and filters them in the browser; Add asset loads 500 premises, 500 units and 500 meters the same way. The kit's type-ahead filters whatever list it is handed, so at a tenant with 1,247 buildings — the figure Add units' own comment gives — every building after the 200th cannot be found, and nothing says so. That is the unpaged-list shape CLAUDE.md forbids at the top of T5. The raise form types into the server's search instead.

RULED 2026-09-24 · raised from an account or an asset, the form arrives filled

PO, verbatim: “now there are screens missing for the forms where service orders are raised from accounts and from assets- the forms should be auto filled by the information , just the first screen needs in the doc for both”. Our reading, recorded rather than asked: both doors open the same raise — 1·4a's three steps — and only step 1 differs. What the door already knows is filled and fixed, in a panel that says which door this is; what the clerk still decides stays a field. Steps 2 and 3 are 1·4b and 1·4c unchanged. The Accounts blueprint already does this for move-in: “Both reach the same wizard, so the step says which one it is on.”

⚠ Measured · the account's button opens an empty form

The account's Work tab already has ⚡ Raise work here, top right. It opens the raise from Work with nothing in it — no account, no address — so the clerk types the address again. It is filed: DEF-WRK-4752, open since 10 Sep, and its own comment says why it was left that way: a link that looked pre-filled would be a lie. The raise form reads nothing from the address bar, and it sends a building and nothing finer — the job never names the account it is for, although work_orders.account_id exists and the raise accepts it.

What the account fills

The account and its holder, its building and flat — walked account → unit → premises, hard rule 8 — its category and status, and its services. A template that names an asset type then lists the account's own assets of that type and the template's service: for a water meter exchange that is W-5000 alone, so it is ticked for you. E-5000 is electric and is not listed. The job stores the account, the building, the flat and the asset.

Why the filled values are facts and not locked boxes

The door decides them, so nothing on this screen may change them — a greyed-out box invites a click that does nothing. The product already shows a fixed value as a fact in a panel (the confirm step, the Accounts blueprint's The account block), so that is what is drawn. To raise the same job somewhere else, start from Work.

A master account names a building, not a flat — our reading

⚠ WHY THIS IS NOT DANGER TIER, AND WHY IT STILL CARRIES A CONSEQUENCE

B14 rule 6 puts the danger tier on destructive commits. Accepting destroys nothing — it turns a service on and a reading into a meter read. Where the two lists are

Crews is 4·1b and Contractors 4·1c, right after 4·1a. Their forms are 4·1d and 4·1e.

RULED 2026-09-24 · Technicians, Crews and Contractors — three lists, not one table

PO, on 4·1, verbatim: “here user is unable to understand the crew and the technicians - can you make it simple to understand for the user - as one table is confusing.” So the page takes the Parts page's own switch — Technicians · Crews · Contractors, each with its count — and each view lists one kind of thing with its own columns: a technician's crew, a crew's members, a contractor's hours. ⚠ THIS SUPERSEDES THE LAST SENTENCE OF BR-WRK-028 (CONFIRMED): “A crew and a contractor are rows in the same table as a person.” The database never did that — people are in technicians, crews and contractors in crews — so the sentence only ever described the screen, and the screen is what changed. The rest of the rule stands: a technician is a profile beside a login, never a second one.

Three sentences leave the page

The closing note — A crew and a contractor are rows in the same table as a person. Whoever the work is offered to, the skill match is the same test. — explains the mix that confused, and is rationale, which B14 rule 33 puts at zero words on screen. The footer's 7 rows · 4 people, 2 crew, 1 contractor is now the switch's counts. And the explainer's Dispatch only offers a technician whose skills match the template has been false since your ruling of 23 Sep: the match advises and never blocks.

One button per view, named for what the view lists

Technicians: + Add crew member. Crews: + Add a crew, with + Add crew member beside it. Contractors: + Add a contractor. The server already takes both kinds (POST /work/crews with a kind); a button called Add a crew that also made contractors would be the same muddle again.

RULED 2026-09-24 · a way in to add a crew member, and the add drawn

PO, on 4·1, verbatim: “here there in this crew section show the wireframes of how crew members are added. also give an navigation from this page to add crew member.” So + Add crew member sits top right on the Crews page (B14 rule 2) and opens 4·1a.

How a crew member is added — measured 24 Sep, and answered in chat the same day

A crew member is a technician profile that names a crew, and a profile always sits on an existing login. Three steps: invite the person in Settings → Users & roles, which makes the login and gives it a role; make them a technician — POST /work/technicians, built and called by no screen; and name the crew, which today can only happen in that same call. Nothing on screen or on the server moves an existing technician to another crew. ⚠ An invited field technician cannot yet set a password (F30), so all four demo technicians are still Invited.

Which roles can be a crew member — any, today

The product has four roles: System Admin, Billing Clerk, Executive and Field technician. The only checks are that the login exists, is not deactivated and is not already a technician, so any role can join a crew — which is why the picker shows each person's role beside the name. A Field technician's login opens the phone only; the other three open both. The job title on the Crews list (Senior technician) is text the utility types and grants nothing. Restricting crews to Field technicians is one server check and one filter on the picker, if you want it.

⚠ Measured · who is on a crew is shown nowhere

The Crews list has no crew column, a crew's row — Field crew A (2) — opens nothing, and the technician page never names its crew. The (2) is a number typed in, not a count: Field crew A holds D. Ortiz and R. Patel, and nothing keeps the two in step. So the new Crew column reads both ways: a person's crew, and a crew's people.

⚠ NFR-3 IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT HOUSEKEEPING

The instruction about later tiers is NEGATIVE: nobody may add a per-tenant cap, an unpaginated list or an account maximum that would have to be removed when T4 arrives. An in-memory page is exactly that, written in a form that passes every test at seven rows.

RULED 2026-09-24 · a way in to add a crew member, and the add drawn

PO, on 4·1, verbatim: “here there in this crew section show the wireframes of how crew members are added. also give an navigation from this page to add crew member.” So + Add crew member sits top right on the Crews page (B14 rule 2) and opens 4·1a.

Which roles can be a crew member — any, today

The product has four roles: System Admin, Billing Clerk, Executive and Field technician. The only checks are that the login exists, is not deactivated and is not already a technician, so any role can join a crew — which is why the picker shows each person's role beside the name. A Field technician's login opens the phone only; the other three open both. The job title on the Crews list (Senior technician) is text the utility types and grants nothing. Restricting crews to Field technicians is one server check and one filter on the picker, if you want it.

⚠ The empty page names a tab that does not exist

Its helper reads Technicians are invited in Settings → Team. The tab is called Users & roles. The dialog's link names the real one and goes there.

T. Brooks is the one illustration

The other seven names are the demo's real logins, in the order the server gives them, with their real roles. The demo has no new starter to add, so the person being added is invented and marked as such here.

DECIDED 2026-09-24 · a contractor's people close their own jobs on the phone

The office never completes a job (ruling 18), and a contractor had no way onto the phone, so its jobs could never be completed. The PO left the choice to us — “u decide”. Phone logins: each of the firm's people is invited with a phone-only login and added on 4·1a with the contractor as their crew, and a job given to the contractor reaches each of their phones. The alternative — the office typing in what the contractor reported — would reopen ruling 18 for one kind of job. A firm that will not use the app: give the job to one of your own technicians, who checks the work and closes it. Written up in the field-app document (T-34, P2.10).

⚠ A contractor has no phone or email on file

No column holds how to reach a contractor, so a job given to Redline Meter Services reaches nobody the product can name. Phone and Email are drawn as new fields; they need columns (P3.53).

The skill advice reads what a crew or contractor can do from crew_skills, and nothing writes it — no screen and no endpoint. What the page's words mean — answered in chat on 24 Sep

What your crews fit, and what each one costs. — the list of parts field crews install, each with the price of one: a price list, never a stock list (no counts, reorder levels or locations, ruled 4 Sep). A template names the parts a job needs; they are copied onto each job; closing the job turns parts × price, plus labour, into its cost. Register is that list. Issue log records parts handed out to a crew or a job, and returns as new lines. Arrives with parts on jobs. is why the Issue log button is grey — and it is out of date: jobs carry their parts (21 lines in the demo), and GET|POST /work/parts/issues are built. Nothing on screen reads or writes them, so the log is empty.

⚠ FOUR OF THE FIVE FAULTS HERE ARE THE SAME SHAPE

Built, not wired. The endpoint is mounted, tested and audited; nothing opens it. This is hard-won law 2, and G13 — the gate written for it — asks whether a prop is passed, not whether a route has a door. Five of the beta's nineteen defects are this shape, and they are the cheapest fixes on the whole list.

⚠ CORRECTED 2026-09-24 — this screen was classed KEEP, needing nothing

It was classed Keep on the strength of the 23 Sep capture — which was of a template with nothing in it, so five zeros looked like an honest empty page. A drawing of an empty record cannot show what the record fails to display. Filling a template through the real builder and opening this tab showed five counts over content the page already holds. The same mistake nearly happened on 6·3c, whose first capture was also empty. Lesson: capture a record screen with a full record, or the capture proves nothing.

⚠ The same fault as 6·3h Review, in a second place

Both screens are handed the whole template and both print counts. They should be one component — B14 rule 43: a piece of UI is built as a COMPONENT; standalone code inside a page is not reuse. Task P3.26 builds it once and places it twice.

Why not the builder's editable tables here

This is the record, not the editor. A published template is changed by opening the builder — ✎ Edit on each panel goes straight to that step — so the page stays a page you read, and there is still exactly one place a row can be changed.

How to tell a customer template from an asset template

The question is what the job is done TO, not who is involved. A meter exchange is done to an asset — the meter — at a customer's premises, with the customer told. So the template is an ASSET template, and it still shows the customer's phone. Scope answers the first question; the four ticks answer the second. Today the builder never sends scope, so every template built here is saved as premises — while the seeded Meter set starter is correctly per_asset. Same kind of job, two different answers, depending on who created it.

This entry said the wizard never collects Service. It does — Service*, second field. What it never collects is scope.

This flow uses the shared frame, and that is worth stating

Three of Work's four multi-step flows do. The rule builder is the exception — see 7·2a.

RULED 2026-09-24 · a task can be edited after it is added

PO, on this screen: “here if the users adds a task and then need to correct it there is not edit available there. the user can edit the task also.” It confirms beta observation #6 as a defect — the product does not do what is expected — rather than a change request.

Why in place, and not an edit button that opens a form

Because half the row already works that way. Photo and Must do are edited by clicking them, in the row. A pencil button beside them would make one row answer two ways — tick these, but open a form for those. The add row is inline too. So the smallest fix is also the most consistent one: the name and the minutes behave like their neighbours.

Editing is safe — a job already raised keeps the task it was given

Every work order carries its own copy of the template's tasks (work_order_tasks, the same four fields plus who ticked it and when). So correcting a task here never changes a job already issued — a technician is never told halfway through a job that the list has changed. On a template that is already published, the correction is saved as a draft and Publish makes the next version; jobs raised after that get the corrected wording.

⚠ “Details” is not a field a task has

Observation #6 asked to edit a task's name, time, or details. A task row stores exactly four things — name, minutes, photo required, must do — and no description or instruction text at all. If a task should carry instructions (“isolate at the main before touching”), that is a new column and a migration — a change, not a fix, and it is OPEN until you say which you meant.

RULED 2026-09-24 · every row added in the builder can be edited

PO, verbatim: “in the work order templates in the new template creation form there should be edit option for wherever the data is added like in the safety step in the materials in the readings wherever there is the data added there should be edit available to the user”. It covers the five list steps — Safety, Tasks, Materials, Readings and Help — and closes the question 6·3c left open about whether to fix Tasks alone.

The pattern, measured across all five steps

Every checkbox in the builder already edits in place; every text or number cell does not. Of eighteen columns across the five steps, the five checkboxes work and thirteen cells are plain text. Twelve of those become editable. One stays read-only on purpose: a material's unit comes with the part (see 6·3d). ⚠ This said twelve locked cells until 24 Sep — a search missed the Materials Part cell because the code writes it across several lines. Driving the screen with real rows found it.

RULED 2026-09-24 · help can be an uploaded document or a video link

PO, on this screen: “user should be able to upload docs, or can add youtube video links. there is no upload button and any links fields”. Confirmed in the running app — neither exists, in the add row or anywhere else in the step.

⚠ The phone half is already built for documents — and not for links

The phone's help list has three branches: a phone number becomes tap to call, a document with a stored file becomes open, and anything else is plain text. So a stored document will start working on the phone the day the builder can store one. A link will not — it would reach the technician as text they cannot tap. One change, two surfaces, and the phone half is the one that gets forgotten: it is task P3.25 here and screen T-28 in the field-app document.

What we decided, and why — none of it needed a ruling

Any https address, not YouTube alone — a utility's own training page or a manufacturer's manual is as useful as a video, and the author is the utility's own staff. https only, validated when typed. A YouTube address is recognised and badged ▶ Video, so a technician knows before tapping that it will play. No migration: the kind column is plain text and the address fits the existing where column.

⚠ The screen's own promise becomes false the day a link exists

Under the heading, the product says of every help row: “Carried on the phone and available with no signal.” True of every row today, and never true of a video. It is correct now, so no check will ever flag it — it only goes wrong on the day the Link kind lands, which is exactly how a sentence outlives its reason. P3.25 changes it in the same commit: Documents work with no signal; links need one. Found by looking at the drawing, not by reading the code.

⚠ A video needs a signal; a document should not

The field app is built to work in a basement. An uploaded document can be kept on the phone for offline use; a video cannot. So every link carries needs a signal on the phone, and a template whose only help is a video leaves a technician with nothing underground. Not refused — said.

The pattern, measured across all five steps

Every checkbox in the builder already edits in place; every text or number cell does not. Of eighteen columns across the five steps, the five checkboxes work and thirteen cells are plain text. Twelve of those become editable. One stays read-only on purpose: a material's unit comes with the part (see 6·3d). ⚠ This said twelve locked cells until 24 Sep — a search missed the Materials Part cell because the code writes it across several lines. Driving the screen with real rows found it.

RULED 2026-09-24 · every process can be set from the rule form

PO, on this screen: “now update the rule form as every process should be able to set from the form. update the document and the wireframes” — said after being shown the list of every way a work order is raised, eighteen rows. Thirteen of them are processes a rule can be set on; the note below accounts for the other five, one by one.

The thirteen, with what each one does

Not rules — a person deciding: A clerk raises a job in Work · A clerk raises a job from an asset · A clerk raises a job from an account. A rule cannot fire on a decision somebody else is making, so these stay doors.

How eighteen became thirteen — nothing dropped

Three are doors, not events — a clerk raising a job in Work, from an asset, from an account. Two rows were the same moment as another row: ⚠ “a move-in or move-out is completed” — CORRECTED 24 Sep: the list shown to you said the existing trigger covers both. It reads move-ins only (customers_seam.completed_occupancies filters kind = move_in), so it IS the move-in row, and move-out is its own process. The seeded rule named Move-in / move-out has never fired on a move-out. And “a payment is received after a disconnection” is the reconnection moment itself — the clerk's paid, awaiting a visit act — so it is one process, for the reason in the next note.

Three ways a process acts — decided here, not put back to you

Overnight, by itself — six processes where no clerk is standing in the moment: a notice expiring, a reading run, an asset's date. That is BR-WRK-033 exactly as signed. Ticked on the clerk's screen — six moments where a clerk IS standing in it and the screen already offers the job. BR-WRK-055, CONFIRMED: “No visit needed is a recorded choice.” Worked: Sarah Miller moves out and sends a photograph of her meter; the clerk unticks the final read. A rule that raised overnight regardless would send a crew to read a meter that has been read. So the rule's job arrives ticked, the clerk can untick it, and nothing is raised twice. WS-29 already draws this state — its first option is ticked, and nothing in the product ticks it today. Shapes the retry — one process the product already raises by signed rule (BR-WRK-054, the retry of a failed job); the rule sets its priority, assignee and escalation, never a second job. Why this was not asked: it keeps both signed rules whole. Raising overnight on a screen moment would override a clerk's recorded choice, and that would be a supersession for you to make.

⚠ A payment alone never books a reconnection — and the list shown to you said it could

BR-PAY-036, CONFIRMED: “A payment is ALWAYS accepted and acceptance NEVER auto-changes account status — restoration stays an explicit, audited staff action.” Worked: A-11340 owes $8,315.00 including the $75.00 reconnection fee. A cheque clears it on Monday. A rule that booked the crew on the payment would have the meter back on by Tuesday — and the cheque can come back on Thursday. So this process works through the clerk's reconnect act: the rule's visit arrives ticked on that screen. ⚠ CORRECTED 24 Sep: the list said reconnecting after payment was “exactly what rules are for”; without the clerk's act it is exactly what a signed rule forbids. It answers OQ-WRK-1726's first question — yes, it is a rule we want — in the only shape the signed rule allows. The register still reads OPEN: this session writes nothing to the repository.

⚠ Fixing the labels alone would switch on a leak rule that catches 98 meters — 51 of them electric

Measured 24 Sep, running the continuous-flow reader with the seeded settings (3 reads in a row, minimum 0): 98 of the demo's 128 meters — 47 water and 51 electric. An electric meter shows use every period, so to this reader every household is a leak. It has never raised a job only because its label is refused (DEF-WRK-4096). So the label fix lands with the Service setting and the unit — task P3.33 — or the first night after it, the dispatcher finds 98 jobs. And the minimum is a bare number compared against kWh and kgal alike: hard rule 3 — consumption always with its unit. Limited to water, the count is 47; that is the figure the Review's preview would show before anyone switches it on.

The estimate-limit process has no number of its own

BR-MET-027, CONFIRMED: a third missed read in a row forces a field visit. The limit lives in Meter-read settings — 2 in a row by default, and a utility that sets 3 gets 3. A second figure on the rule would let the two disagree: estimating stops at 2, the rule waits for 3, and the meter gets neither an estimate nor a visit. So the form shows the limit read-only, with where to change it.

The certification-due-soon process is the drawn Backflow rule

WS-26 draws Backflow test due firing on “Certification due within 30 days”. The engine can only answer already past, so the seed ships that rule OFF and says why in its own code. The new process is the same reader read ahead of the date — and the rule can then be switched on. The 30 is the drawing's figure and stays an illustration (B14 rule 37); the utility types its own.

Beta reports—
RULED 2026-09-24 · all seven escalations on the rule; reminders live in Notifications

PO, verbatim, on the table put to them in chat: “add all these escalations in the wireframe. if reminders can be managed in notifications then remove if needed”. So step 4 is Escalation — seven rows, each on or off, with its hours where it has any, who is told and the message it sends — and the step's old name, Reminders & escalation, goes with the reminders. Reminders move to Notifications, where the customer's already are (Appointment window, Technician on the way); the staff reminders — a certificate expiring, a job waiting for approval, the technician's day — become messages there (P3.59).

Who is told follows a signed rule — our reading, recorded rather than asked

BR-NOT-021 (CONFIRMED): a staff message goes to whoever started the action, plus every System Admin when something has gone wrong; and no rule may choose its own recipients — the product states the policy and draws no picker. An escalation is something going wrong, so each row names its person — whoever raised, assigned, scheduled or held the job, which at a small utility is the dispatcher — and every System Admin, which is the supervisor. There is no Dispatcher or Supervisor role: the four are System Admin, Billing Clerk, Executive and Field technician. Choosing a person or a role per escalation instead would change BR-NOT-021 — one sentence from you.

One message exists; six are new

Only SLA breach is in the notification catalogue today (in-app and email), and nothing sends it. The other six — Job not assigned, Job not accepted, Running late (to staff, and to the customer), Hold overdue, Job failed, Approval overdue — are new messages there, in all eleven languages, worded in Notifications and nowhere else (BR-NOT-017, one home).

Three rows need something that does not exist yet

Technician hasn't accepted needs the phone's accept (field-app P2.2). On hold too long needs a hold to carry its return date (P0.3, P5.2). Running late needs the phone to say it is on site (field-app P4.1). They are drawn switched on because the ruling asks for all seven; each fires from the day its precondition lands.

Two clocks on one job — which is which

A job's priority already carries hours — on the demo Urgent 4 · High 8 · Normal 72 · Low 168 — and they say when the WORK must be done. The rule's escalation says when a job nobody has picked up is shouted about. Different questions, so both stay: after the rule's hours with no acceptance, the job goes on the at-risk board (P5.3) and the back office is told (P6.2). Blank still means nothing escalates — the product's own sentence, kept.

⚠ Three of the five steps do nothing today

The raise reads the template, the rule's name and its priority — and nothing else (rules._raise_one). Assignment, notifications and escalation are cleaned, saved and served back, and never read. rules_models.py says of them “each is READ by the raise”; hard-won law 1 — a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. A supervisor who sets all five steps gets a job raised by step 1 alone.

What reminders and escalations should exist — answered in chat 24 Sep

Asked on 7·2d. Today the step holds one box, and nothing reads it. Reminders: the customer the day before the visit (appointment_window exists, on booking only); the technician's jobs for the day (no message — the phone's push is not sent yet); on the way (technician_on_the_way exists); a certificate expiring in 30 days (no message); a job waiting for approval (no message). Escalations: nobody assigned after N hours (the box's own purpose — no message); not accepted by the technician; running late at the end of the window; overdue past the due time (sla_breach exists); on hold past its return date; a failed job; not approved in time. Three of the twelve have a message in Notifications, and none is sent today — every field-work message is still marked as waiting for the Work module. Proposed shape: one row each — a tick, the hours, who is told — with the wording kept in Notifications, as step 3 already does.

Why the Review states tonight's count

B14 rule 11 — a consequence before the commit. Activating a rule is reversible; the jobs it raises tonight are not undone by switching it off. 98 is the number that should stop a supervisor, and today nothing shows it. A read-only run of the chosen reader answers it, writes nothing, and is the same query the sweep makes.

⚠ Fixing the labels alone would switch on a leak rule that catches 98 meters — 51 of them electric

Measured 24 Sep, running the continuous-flow reader with the seeded settings (3 reads in a row, minimum 0): 98 of the demo's 128 meters — 47 water and 51 electric. An electric meter shows use every period, so to this reader every household is a leak. It has never raised a job only because its label is refused (DEF-WRK-4096). So the label fix lands with the Service setting and the unit — task P3.33 — or the first night after it, the dispatcher finds 98 jobs. And the minimum is a bare number compared against kWh and kgal alike: hard rule 3 — consumption always with its unit. Limited to water, the count is 47; that is the figure the Review's preview would show before anyone switches it on.

04 · Journeys — what happened when the app was driven

Two independent passes. A code walk drove all 24 routes in the running app on 23 September; a person using the product reported 34 observations the same day. Where they agree the finding is strongest; where they disagree, both are recorded.

J1 · The 34 beta observations

In the reporter's own words, verbatim. A report paraphrased is a report argued with.

A report is a defect by default

PO ruling 2026-09-10: “CR is change in product, defect is product does not do what is expected.” The burden is on us to prove something is a change request, never the other way round — filing our misunderstanding as a “change” quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement.

Of these 34: 19 are defects, 5 are genuine change requests, 6 confirm a finding this document had already filed, 1 is correct by design, and 2 need a re-walk before anybody builds.

J2 · What the product says it cannot do

Carried whole from the earlier edition. Every string in which the product refuses something, in its own words — and the eight that hold a visible control are the ones that rot, because a refusal is written once and outlives its reason silently.

Built from the product's own user-facing copy — the sentences a person reads when something cannot be done — not from my impressions. 24 stated absences, of which 8 hold a control the user can see and cannot use. Each gets exactly one ruling, by the same test throughout:

A recorded ruling that a thing waits makes it OUT OF SCOPE, with the ruling quoted. No ruling makes it a SPECIFICATION naming what it waits on.

The eight that hold a visible control

What is absentThe product's wordsScreenRuling
Parts Issue log segment“Arrives with parts on jobs.”11SPEC W-07 — held against wave N, which has landed
Approvals empty CTA“The field closes these, not here.”08SPEC W-05 — destination is live
Performance empty CTA“Close a job first”28SPEC W-05 — destination is live
Approvals row 👁 with no build“This job has no build.”08SPEC W-05 — order detail shipped in wave H
Crews Add a technician“Invite them in Settings first.”09OUT OF SCOPE — a technician's login belongs to identity and Work may not create one (BR-WRK-002, and G78 fails the merge). The refusal names where to go.
Labour rates Add a rate“Adding arrives shortly”—OUT OF SCOPE — that screen is outside this audit's scope; listed for completeness only
Template Audit tab“The change history opens with the next release.”13OUT OF SCOPE — the trail exists in audit_log; the reader is a named later wave, and the tab is honest about it
Runbooks work row action“No screen fixes this”—OUT OF SCOPE — a work.* key rendered outside this module

Where the rule was close, and how it decided

The Crews “Add a technician” button and the Approvals “Open work orders” button look identical — both greyed, both with a reason, both written by careful people citing the same rule. The test separates them cleanly. Crews is out of scope: a recorded ruling says Work may not create a login, a gate enforces it, and the refusal points at the place that can. Approvals is a specification: no ruling says that button must stay dead, its destination has been live since wave H, and it sits one tab away on the same screen. The difference is not the wording or the care — it is whether anything was ever ruled.

Dead copy — strings in all eleven catalogues that nothing renders

KeyThe string nobody seesWhy it is orphaned
work.templates.empty.ctaReason“The template builder opens with the next release.”The builder shipped. Its live CTA passes no ctaReason; the string was left behind in every locale.
work.orders.empty.ctaReason“Not from this screen yet.”Removed from the component when the wizard landed — with a comment saying why — and not from the catalogues.

work.mobile.pane.held“Arrives in the next release.”Live and unreachable: the phone's held-panes register is now empty, because waves K and L each deleted a pane's row in the same commit that mounted it. The machinery is kept deliberately so the next hold inherits the expiry test — this is the one mechanism in Work that does holds properly.
Dead copy is cheap to leave and costs a translator in eleven languages. But note what the fourth row shows: the phone's held-panes register is empty because every hold it carried expired correctly and was removed in the commit that made it untrue. That is the behaviour the Parts segment and the two dead CTAs are missing, and it already exists in this module — thirty files away.

“The map renders blank over served data.” I read the map's innerText, got nothing, and was about to file it. The DOM said otherwise — sixteen text-free pin buttons, correctly positioned. Across the module boundary

Carried whole from the earlier edition. Four questions asked of every crossing: does any module write another's tables, does every crossing go through a seam, does one fact have two homes, does the same thing have two names.

Work is the eleventh code module. It owns crews, technicians, skills, certifications, parts, work orders, templates, assignments, schedules, rules and labour rates; it reads assets, connections, accounts, meter reads, areas and users through one read-only seam file per module; and it writes none of them. Four questions, asked from above.

1 · Does any module write another's tables?

No. This is the cleanest thing about the module.

I searched every .py under apps/work, excluding seams, tests and migrations, for imports of the other ten modules, and every seam for .create(), .update(), .save() and .delete(). Not one cross-module write exists. Eight seam files, each read-only. metering_seam.py even carries a note asserting that apps/work/** contains no MeterRead.objects.create.

2 · Does every crossing go through a seam?

From → toThroughReturnsGrade
work → meteringseams/metering_seam.py — connection(), premises(), work_order()dictHEALTHY
work → meteringseams/metering_seam.py — open_work_orders_queryset(), open_orders_at_unit_queryset(), search_work_orders_queryset()a raw QuerySetLEAKY
work → customersseams/customers_seam.py — eight named functionsdict / list[dict]HEALTHY
work → identityseams/identity_seam.py — user(), may(), staff_user_choices()dict / boolHEALTHY
work → assetsseams/assets_seam.pydict / listHEALTHY
work → payments · billing · notifications · tenancyone seam file eachdict / list[dict]HEALTHY
work → tenancywork_documents.py:73, evidence.py:68, mobile.py:320 — document_models and document_store imported directly—LEAKY — a read that bypasses the seam. Document storage is arguably platform rather than a peer module, and nothing rules it either way.
work → meteringsample_field_work.py:746 — apps.metering.connections imported directly—LEAKY — and G78 says so, in red, since 2026-09-16
The three queryset seams are LEAKY by the test this document applies throughout: grade on what the seam hands back, not what its docstring says it does. These return a live QuerySet, so a caller can filter, join, slice — and write — through it, and the boundary the seam exists to draw is gone. In fairness the docstring is candid (“A READ: the selector orders, searches and slices it and writes nothing”), the selector does exactly that, and this is the shape that makes the Orders list's SQL pagination possible — which is the one list in Work that pages correctly. It is a real trade-off, not an oversight; it is graded LEAKY because the grade is about what is possible, not what is currently done.

3 · Does one fact have two homes?

No. The address rule is obeyed, and visibly so.

Hard rule 8 puts an address on premises and nowhere else; every other entity walks to it. open_work_orders_queryset() joins four anchors — the connection's premises, the order's own premises_id, the unit's premises, and the account — precisely so that the Premise column can be derived rather than stored. No work-order table carries an address column. The map's coordinates come from the same walk, so the map and the envelope cannot disagree.

4 · Does the same thing have two names?

ConceptWork calls itElsewhereVerdict
A jobWork order, WO-0001Job queue (customers) · Open work (assets)CONSISTENT — the surfaces differ, the noun does not
Held vs in the booksRecorded (Performance cost tile)B14 rule 34's pairCONSISTENT
A person who does the workTechnician · Crew · Contractor“workforce” in search destinations onlyMINOR — workforce is an internal search key a user never sees; no screen shows it
Of the four cross-module questions, two found nothing — no module writes another's tables, and no fact has two homes. Saying so explicitly matters more than the two that did find something, because an absent heading reads as an unasked question.
The dependency that gates the most, and it is not ours

A tile source for the map. It is the only item in this document that no amount of engineering unblocks: a third-party dependency with a key and a monthly cost, and a decision only the Product Owner can make. Clustering, the pin destination and the key can all be built without it — and the screen stays a set of marks on a blank canvas until somebody buys a map.

06 · Register

65 screens drawn — 51 update, 1 keep, 0 remove — plus three named in the plan and not drawn. And 223 clerk capabilities: 47 built, 26 partial, 150 missing. These reconcile with the generated manifest below; if they disagree, the manifest is right and the prose is stale.

Every repo id reads S-NEW, and three screens are deliberately not drawn

Never invent a repo id. S-NEW means a number must be allocated through 10-scripts/allocate.py, which asks the remote rather than this checkout — because two lanes counting locally both get the same answer.

The at-risk board, the schedule board and bulk raise are committed as tasks and not drawn. Drawing them would mean inventing a layout for screens nobody has specified, and an invented drawing in a document like this is read as a decision. They are named so the 20 capabilities that currently live nowhere have somewhere to go.
